verdict.rationale: Logseq is fundamentally local-first — data lives in local Markdown/EDN files with no forced cloud, matching 'privacy-first, open-source knowledge base' (logseq-docs-23) and exports to plain files (logseq-docs-8/30). Community members confirm running it purely locally or syncing via their own GitHub repo instead of vendor sync (logseq-comm-1, logseq-comm-7). However, there is no official self-hosted sync backend: Logseq's own multi-device Sync is a paid vendor cloud service (logseq-docs-10, logseq-docs-28), and a user explicitly wished for self-hosting as a website with an open, long-unresolved GitHub issue (logseq-comm-20), showing the vendor never shipped a self-hostable server option. Missing for 10: an official self-hosted sync/server component operated by the user, and stronger evidence of robust single-device local-only workflows at scale (performance complaints in logseq-comm-5/6).
